parts.text: 5 Three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.

ms.label: 5(a)
ms.text:
1 mark each for any two of:
•
has a definite shape / does not take the shape of the container
•
has a definite volume / fixed volume
•
does not spread over surface / does not flow
•
cannot be compressed

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Complete Table 5.1 to show the separation and arrangement of particles in a solid and a gas. Table 5.1 physical state separation of particles arrangement of particles solid gas [4]

ms.label: 5(b)
ms.text:
solid:
separation of particles: touching / close together (1)
arrangement: regular / fixed pattern (1)
gas:
separation of particles: far apart / long way from each other (1)
arrangement: irregular / no (particular) arrangement / random (1)

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Draw a line from each statement to the correct change of state. carbon dioxide gas turns into liquid carbon dioxide ice turns into water liquid nitrogen changes into nitrogen gas statement melting boiling condensing change of state [2]

ms.label: 5(c)
ms.text:
all three correct = 2 marks
one correct = 1 mark
carbon dioxide gas turns into liquid carbon dioxide: condensing
ice turns into water: melting
liquid nitrogen changes into nitrogen gas: boiling
